verdict.tagline: A short, harrowing descent into surreal psychological horror.
for_you_if: you appreciate surreal psychological horror narratives
you enjoy striking retro aesthetics and strong atmosphere
you want an intense experience playable in one sitting
not_for_you_if: you dislike walking simulators with minimal mechanics
you find strict puzzle sequences and mazes frustrating

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Reviewers note the brief single sitting length and retro visuals while pointing out frustrating maze segments and strict puzzle ordering.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as very short, taking around two hours to finish in a single sitting.

citations.review_text: I could refund it, it only took me an hour and half to beat the game, but I won't because the game is fantastic and I want to support the devs. Even if I had gotten it at full retail price it's still worth it to support projects like this. Don't let the internet cornballs who latched themselves onto this game make you avoid playing it, it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ excellent.

Reviews painted it as a masterpiece of a game, but in reality it’s a primitive walking simulator with a “deep story” - a completely linear short game (about three hours). After two hours of wandering around a small ship without my actions having any influence on what was happening, I decided to request a refund and watch the last hour of a playthrough to see what the ending was. The main twist turned out to be predictable, and overall I didn’t like the story. The psychological horror here is basically cobbled together from cliches and psychedelic imagery that don’t impress, and some moments are just irritating. In the end, we’re left with a simple story in the form of an overrated walking sim.

Interesting game, sort of like a point and click adventure, good story and psychological horror. Took about 2hrs to finish. 
Although honestly, not to be a prude, but they went a bit overboard on the gore/visceral/grossness/etc stuff especially in the last quarter. Tied to that are some pretty sensitive themes [spoiler] abortion [/spoiler] that add to how uncomfortable the game is. 

[u] [b] TLDR: [/b] Genuinely probably damaging for your psyche to consume media like this. But I suppose that means its an effective psychological horror huh? [/u]

Legit knew absolutely nothing about this game getting into it and it was really freaking good. I am not going to say anything in this review as I recommend playing it with no prior knowledge but it is twisted and messed up but really well written. It had me on multiple occasions inspired by the amount of creativity and imagery used in such an unwavering to the characters and plot sort of way. It’s short so it’s not really taking out time for a JRPG it’s something you can finish in one sitting. Go for it!

claims.claim: The game features retro-style, blocky, or PlayStation 1-esque graphics combined with surreal imagery and sound design.

citations.review_text:
Mouthwashing is a very good game that does a lot with very little. Mostly it's just walking around to solve minor puzzles so you can unlock further conversations; the story being the selling point. It's very bleak, and difficult to discuss without spoilers, but I found every character to be excellent and the developing plot to be just the kind of material I like. It was sad, and left me thinking after the experience was over. It's helped along by really interesting visuals and sound design; and though I kept thinking "this would be an awesome movie" it really knew how to best make use of its format as a video game. 

I think the occasional input to solve a simple puzzle or just to refocus your attention was really helpful. It kept the horror alive, so I was kind of scared right from the onset and all throughout. By making use of its retro-esque graphics and fondness for pseudo-glitches, the game was able to blend a narrative well alongside creepy sequences kind of like a dream or hallucination. At some points I was amazed by the clever use of abrasive textures or fuzziness used to conceal aspects of the environment or to hide revealing information for later, alongside the constantly shifting perspectives. There was a few points where it became more "gamelike" in that you had to navigate a small maze or avoid some pitfall, but it never went on so long that I felt frustrated or taken out of the experience. 

Mouthwashing is just really worth playing for any horror fan, as it doesn't require much skill and the story is presented efficiently. I can see why the reviews are so phenomenal, and I agree entirely. One of the best narrative-horror walking simulators you can play.

This game messed me up. I wasn’t sure what to think at first. The blocky, retro-style graphics and surreal, dream-like sequences make a weird first impression, but the game completely pulls you in. And despite the title, it leaves an incredibly bitter taste in your mouth.
This is one of the few games I’ve walked away from feeling genuinely horrified, and the story has been living in my head rent-free ever since. It’s hard to say more without spoiling anything, but I can say this without a doubt: the antagonist of this story is one of the most utterly irredeemable characters I have ever seen written. Yet, they are so masterfully developed that you end up hating them all the more for it.
Gameplay-wise, it’s not super complicated. It’s mostly exploratory, clicking around to see what changes and solving light puzzles, but every single mechanic actively supports and builds onto the narrative. Same with the music and graphics. 
If you like psychological horror that stays with you, I easily recommend this.

first and foremost [spoiler] ♥♥♥♥ YOU JIMMY [/spoiler]

subvert your expected storytelling at almost every step, psychological horrifying great plus for the sound / playstation 1 esque art direction from a random horror indie game

(9/10)

One of the best horror games ive ever played. Doesnt bombard you with jumpscares and when they do happen, they get you good. The story is immaculate and the art style just fits the vibe so well. Well done Wrong Organ, you made a literal masterpiece. Evidence that video games are an art form

You'll be walking around trying to find what it is that the game wants you to do, and then figure out that it was something that was almost right next to you. In that sense, this game can be a bit frustrating, but I would say this is my only gripe. Other than that, this is easily one of the most unique games I've played in recent memory.

This is remarkably poor as both a game and a story. It's a walking simulator, which normally I'm not a fan of but there are some I like. There are a tiny handful of segments where you have to use an item or enter a code, but there may as well be no actual gameplay. In terms of a walking simulator it's poor at that too. There's again only a scant handful of visual vignettes that leave a faint impression, the rest of the walking is back and forth through dark, boring corridors. 

As for the story, I tried to interpret it charitably but I don't think flashing the theme of the game "Take Responsibility" repeatedly across the screen is a good way to communicate meaning. I read through some other interpretations of the story online and was floored by how much people have invented meaning where no evidence for it exists. I'll briefly comment on specifics in spoilers:
[spoiler]Any meaning in the story is greatly overshadowed by the simple premise that a man impregnated a woman, and decided to kill everyone instead of take responsibility. Everything that follows from this psychotic to-the-point-of-absurd action is kind of lost in that context. Anya kills herself and Swansea gets drunk, yeah what else were they supposed to do? People commented on the characters too but the reality is we learn barely enough to make most of the characters more than one dimensional. "Our worst moments don't define us" is another theme flashed irritatingly before the players eyes constantly, but we never learn of any of the characters worst moments or much about them at all other than basic back story.
Some people also read anti-capitalist themes into this because a freight company was hauling mouthwash and also went bankrupt? What you think a long-haul trucker opens the back of his can and goes "MY GOD! I've just been hauling TOILET PAPER this whole time??" Get a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ grip. What did they think they were hauling the cure for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cancer?[/spoiler]

In summation I would say Mixtape is slight…

The game does have quite a few unique ideas, but sadly the writing falls off pretty hard towards the middle which made me lose interest in the 'main character', The rest of the game then becomes quite a slog as you experience surreal dream sequences, chase scenes and ample body horror through the eyes of that character.

Game starts good and atmospherics, but at some point there is a level where you have to go through a maze while avoiding monster. Total pace and mood killer.
Completely disgracefully and tasteful gamedev choice.
Other than that game is standard storytelling walking simulator.

It expects you to do things in certain order and look for clues, look for prompts and click on the rights things in the right order to progress. The setting is cool, but not my type of game.

A good story, a bad game. Calling this a game is quite misleading if you ask me with little interaction you actually have with most of the segments. Some character are nicely written others aren't but the plot is rather nicely presented and interesting. Gruesome but not scary at all. If it wasn't a small creator I would have ask for a refund.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players praise the non-linear time jumping story and atmospheric retro art style that builds an effective horror experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features a non-linear narrative with time jumps that switch between past and future events.

citations.review_text: This was a tough one to sit through. It is very depressing, very psychological in its horror. I hated the back and forth story telling of past and future events. I don't mind it being used for flashbacks in story telling but this game its every single scene your going back and forth between past and future/present. Not a fan of that. The story is super grim and depressing so be prepared for that I suppose. Otherwise the game has some good retro style art and this game defiantly nails its atmosphere. I give this a middle of the road recommendation if i could, id say a yes for recommendation as it is good for what it is, i just didn't care for the storytelling personally.

Its just alcoholism and stupid stuff ♥♥♥♥ swansea, in actuality very good game i like the idea of constantly going back n forth through the timeline figuring out the story and realizing you got it wrong the entire time and seeing the mental state of the crew changing etc and very good ending :D

The game is well-presented. The art style and care for establishing the environment is top-notch. The narrative is well structured... And generally speaking I'm a fan of walking simulators, and weird unreal environments are my jam.

But I just don't think it's practical to combine seven different possible reasons for why what we're looking at isn't real, [spoiler](seriously, four different reasons for schizophrenic breaks, perspective hopping, and [i]fake[/i] perspective hopping?)[/spoiler] AND expect us to follow the story. At some point it just becomes impossible to know what's supposed to matter. If a character is doing something horrifying, my first reaction shouldn't be "This doesn't gel with anything I know about this character, doesn't seem to be revealing anything coherent, and I bet this is another thing that's not going to come up again. Did the dev just feel like adding gore for its own sake?"

I'll upvote because it's otherwise well made and it's great at what it's trying to be, but it's not for me. I had to read a wiki to figure out what was supposedly going on.

I know Mouthwashing is controversial and some people couldn't finish it on account of its subject matter and graphic content. However, I feel the controversy is over-hyped and the game was more weird and unsettling than truly horrific.  I actually had a lot of fun with this surreal and over-the-top descent into madness filled with a variety of tricks and puzzles to mess with the player's head.  One example of these mind-f***s that doesn't spoil the plot is how the scenes change with glitches that made me wonder if the game crashed. So, if you aren't sensitive to moderate levels of gore and themes of self-harm, then don't hold back from experiencing this wild and surreal story. Speaking of story, I like how it switches between different characters' perspectives and points in time that slowly, but progressively reveal how badly things are going for the ship's crew.  I also love the mood set with the PS1-inspired graphics and the sound design too.
Mouthwashing runs almost perfectly out of the box on CachyOS with Proton 11, but there were occasional hitches that typically occurred when rotating the camera/POV. Occasionally playing with a controller would feel clunky and I needed to switch to keyboard and mouse.  Switching controls especially helped with the scene set in an ornate tomb where you have to use a gun and aim quickly. Control response and accuracy doesn't matter for like 90% of the game, though.

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the retro art style and sound design for creating an effective atmospheric and psychological horror experience.

citations.review_text:
Just bought and finished Mouthwashing today and… holy moly. I absolutely loved it.

I’m not usually into horror because I  can’t play jumpscarey games, so I was glad this doesn’t lean heavy into that. I love atmospheric horror. The art, sound design, and pacing all work well to create the constant feeling of dread and unease. It gets under your skin by slowly revealing just how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ everything really is.

It’s short, but I think that works in its favor. It doesn’t overstay its welcome or dilute its impact. It just grabs you, drags you through its increasingly disturbing story, and then leaves you sitting there staring at the screen like: “…what the ♥♥♥♥.”

10/10.

I've been putting off reviewing this game for a little bit because I wasn't really sure what to say.

After I beat the game I kinda sat there like "Did I enjoy that?" and I think that's kinda the best way I can describe how I feel about the game in short.

Mouthwashing certainly isn't a bad game by any means, but I also don't think it's nearly as good as it seems to be hyped up to be.

I had originally thought I was gonna go for 100% achievements for this game as its kinda a mission I've been going on recently to try and 100% every game I truly enjoy going forward (within reason) but after finishing this I felt no urge to press onward to get the remaining ones.

Hopefully I can shed some light as to why, starting with the good things.

I love the general aesthetic of the game, it really does ooze a certain PS1-PS2 type of style that I always really enjoy. It's got really great art and sound direction honestly and some of the scenes are really creative and interesting.

However...the story is a little winky wonky in my opinion and it didn't really hit for me, perhaps that's just a me issue, who knows. But it felt kinda under baked or not really that satisfying of a conclusion? Like the game didn't really have much to actually say in the end beyond "He who shall not be named is an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥."

Which for me personally was just kinda...eh? Like yeah I get it the dude has mental health problems and stuff, but uh...gonna be honest Curly's reaction...or lack there of during the ship crash flashback- actually pulled me out of the immersion entirely, it seems completely out of character for him to just let Jdawg just walk in there alone and pull that ♥♥♥♥ without him saying a single word after he made it pretty clear what he was about to do.

I give it like a 6.5 outta 10?

beautiful experience,interesting story with good characters with absolute peak design and beautiful overall ambiance,art style and sound design.
Especially the art style is scrumptious.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay as minimal, characterizing it primarily as a walking simulator with basic navigation and few interactive mechanics.

citations.review_text: What a bizarre and memorable story. The characters are all so unique in both design and personality. The game covers a sci-fi delivery freight crew as they return home with a shipment. The themes are dark and the gameplay is a dialogue-heavy walking simulator with a few puzzles, and I mean that in the most positive way possible. Three hours is enough time to cover this game at a leisurely pace. I can't wait to see what Wrong Organ comes up with next.
took me roughly 3 hours, mostly a walking simulator, not too original with its scares or surrealism, but is really densely packed with interesting themes and well written characters

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game runs stably on integrated graphics.

citations.review_text: Great game, really enjoyed the way the story is told here by giving you the "answer" first then the question later doing that back and forth story telling really well best use of my 3 hours so far. cant really glaze the game without spoiling it since its so short so just please go ahead and play it. AND, and most importantly. it performs as it looks! stable 90+ fps on my igpu you'd think this should be the norm but somehow most devs put bazillion shaders on top while developing the game on UE5 for that ps1 look.... with the ps6 performance costs.....
